method: NAR 12+2-layer Spec-Drafter drafts k=25 tokens; accept if in target top-β (β=3) and log-prob gap to top-1 ≤ τ (1.0)
upside: relaxed top-β/τ acceptance lets long NAR blocks survive, so ~8 tokens accepted per iteration
method_downside: lossy: output no longer the target's greedy/sampled sequence; β and τ must be tuned per task; separate drafter trained per target (mask-predict)
memory: separate Transformer-base-size drafter; paper reports ~245-555 MB extra at test time
quality: lossy, no drop measured: BLEU 28.93 vs 28.73 AR greedy (WMT14 En-De); ROUGE +0.03 (CNN/DM, BART-base)

method: small model generates; fallback to large model when small-model confidence is low; rollback when large-model cross-entropy to a small token exceeds a threshold
upside: plug-and-play, no training; tokens with small discrepancy are kept, so the large model runs rarely
method_downside: lossy: tokens the large model would not pick are kept; fallback and rollback thresholds must be tuned; small and large models must be aligned (README advises fine-tuning the small model)
memory: not reported; small model (T5/mT5-small class) + its KV (est.)
quality: lossy: 'minimal' quality degradation at up to 2.12x; exact BLEU/ROUGE drop not seen
datasets: IWSLT2017 De-En, WMT14 De-En, XSum, CNN/DM

method: decoding heads + tree attention; accept candidate if target prob > min(ε, δ·exp(−H(p))) instead of rejection sampling
upside: entropy-adaptive threshold accepts more candidates at T>0 than rejection sampling, without a separate drafter
method_downside: lossy at T>0: not the target distribution (reduces to greedy match at T=0); ε, δ are global constants to tune; heads retrained per target
memory: Medusa heads: ResBlock + own vocab projection each, ~0.15B per head on 7B, ~0.7B for 5 heads (est.); no extra KV
quality: lossy at T>0: MT-Bench quality roughly unchanged (unv.)
accepted_tokens: not reported for typical acceptance alone
speed: ~2x wall-time (Vicuna-7B/13B/33B, A100, bs1, MT-Bench, Medusa-1); +10% over greedy on creative tasks with typical acceptance; Medusa-2 2.3-3.6x (unv.)

method: choose the output distribution that maximizes acceptance subject to an f-divergence budget (TV/KL) to the target; link to boosting
upside: explicit, provably optimal acceptance-quality trade-off; cheap data structure (O(sort(n)) build, O(log n) query)
method_downside: lossy: output follows a divergence-bounded proxy, not the target; per-token budget compounds over sequence length; budget must be chosen
memory: none beyond the drafter (est.); per-step sort over the vocabulary
quality: lossy with bounded per-token divergence; measured drop not reported in material seen

method: linear judge head on target last-layer embeddings classifies whether a mismatching draft token is still correct; accept if yes
upside: accepts mismatches that are semantically fine, so ~20 tokens per round with a strong 8B drafter
method_downside: lossy: no guarantee of target distribution; judge needs hand-labeled error annotations and new domains need new labels (OOD drop); needs a strong drafter (Medusa/EAGLE heads unsuitable) and a large target
memory: judge head 16,384 params (405B) / 8,192 (70B), negligible; plus separate Llama-3.1-8B drafter + its KV
quality: lossy: GSM8K ~90% and HumanEval 86.6% ~ target 405B; OOD (code removed from judge data) HumanEval 86.6% -> 80.4%
speed: 8B/405B: 9.7x HF, 3.9x gpt-fast, 129.3 tok/s; 8B/70B: 2x HF, 3x gpt-fast, 141.8 tok/s (H100, 8-bit, bs1)

method: mine 'important' mismatches (substitution changes final answer) offline with target rollouts, train logistic regression on draft+target hidden states, accept unimportant mismatches
upside: removes manual annotation of Judge Decoding; cheap classifier at inference
method_downside: lossy: target distribution not preserved; labels need verifiable tasks (final-answer change) and classifier degrades OOD, so mining is redone per domain; offline mining needs many sequential target passes
memory: logistic regression on concatenated hidden states (~6k params, est.) + Llama-3.2-1B drafter + KV
quality: lossy: ≤1% accuracy drop on GSM8K at ~1.5x more accepted tokens; ~1% drop on LiveCodeBench at ~2x
accepted_tokens: 15+ (GSM8K), 20+ (LiveCodeBench) per cycle, window W=64 (Llama 1B/8B, greedy on GSM8K)
speed: ~2x over standard SD (GSM8K/LiveCodeBench); hardware and batch not specified
llama_results: Llama-3.2-1B -> Llama-3.1-8B: up to 1.5x more accepted tokens at ≤1% GSM8K drop

method: self-supervised judge: label mismatches by semantic preservation score (bidirectional likelihood of replaced vs original token), train logistic regression on target hidden states
upside: no ground-truth answers needed, so labels extend beyond math/code
method_downside: lossy: target distribution not preserved; label threshold τ calibrated on annotated math examples; label creation needs pre-generated target responses and extra scoring passes
memory: logistic regression on target hidden states (~4k params, est.) + 1B/0.5B drafter + KV
quality: lossy: -1.0% average task accuracy (vs -2.7% for AutoJudge)
accepted_tokens: +2.06 accepted tokens/cycle over standard SD (vs +1.96 AutoJudge)
speed: not reported as wall-clock in material seen (V100, T=0)

method: accept draft token if JS divergence between target and draft distributions < threshold T, else standard SD rejection
upside: single knob trades accuracy for speed; T=0 recovers lossless SD
method_downside: lossy for T>0: no quality guarantee; mapping from T to downstream accuracy unknown and task/candidate-length dependent, so T must be calibrated per dataset
memory: none beyond the drafter (Llama-3.1-8B + KV for 70B target)
quality: lossy: ~2% absolute accuracy drop at >5 tok/s over SD (GSM8K, CSQA); ~0% on HumanEval
speed: Llama 8B/70B, 2xA100, bs1: GSM8K 16.8 (SD) -> 19.5 (matched acc.) / 22.0 tok/s; HumanEval 20.5 -> 22.3 / 23.6
llama_results: Llama-3.1 8B->70B: GSM8K 22.0 vs 16.8 tok/s SD at -2.0% acc.

method: verify against a learned mixture of draft and target, weight w_t from a small FFN on both hidden states, trained with REINFORCE++ (task reward + TV acceptance term)
upside: context-dependent weight raises acceptance where mixing is harmless and keeps the target where it matters
method_downside: lossy: samples from learned mixture, not the target; weight net trained per task with RL; needs draft and target hidden states each step and a patched transformers fork
memory: small FFN weight network (size not reported) + Llama-3.2-1B drafter + KV
quality: lossy: 'comparable quality' (ROUGE, accuracy, perplexity); exact drop not seen
accepted_tokens: not reported in material seen (figures only)
speed: not reported in material seen (T=0, 128 tokens on CNN/DM)
llama_results: Llama-3.2-1B -> Llama-3.1-8B (main pair); numbers not seen

method: at a high-entropy mismatch (θ=0.3) open a W=6 window and accept if the target does not diverge again; stacked with prompt-lookup drafting
upside: training-free; accepts semantically correct drafts, so tau 11-18 and robust OOD
method_downside: lossy: not the target's tokens, unsuitable for verbatim reproduction; commit delayed by W tokens; W and θ set empirically
memory: none beyond Llama-3.1-8B drafter + KV (PLD n-gram is free)
datasets: GSM8K, HumanEval, MBPP; OOD: ACP-prog-gen, NIAH-multivalue, MGSM

method: analysis: splits lossy verification into truncation-based (SpecCascade, Medusa typical) and collaborative (lenience, CoS) families, tested with EAGLE-3
upside: single harness and taxonomy for lossy rules; names failure modes
method_downside: n/a (analysis paper); finds truncation rules distort the distribution and collaborative rules degrade unless draft-probability overshoot (q ≥ p/ℓ) is controlled
quality: truncation (SpecCascade) gap to true truncation sampling grows with difficulty: 0.38 pp (GSM8K) to 6.67 pp (AIME)
accepted_tokens: reported as block efficiency; numbers not seen
speed: reported as decoding speed; numbers not seen
datasets: MATH, MBPP+, INCLUDE, BFCL, GSM8K, AIME

method: speculative cascades: cascade deferral rule (Chow, Diff, OPT, Token variants) executed via speculative draft-then-score
upside: keeps cascade cost-quality gains (can beat the large model) with parallel SD-style verification
method_downside: lossy: samples from a deferral-defined mixture, not the large model; plug-in optimal rule needs calibrated confidence; higher total compute than sequential cascades
memory: small model + its KV (T5-small 77M; Gemma 2B/9B for 27B)
quality: lossy by design: matches large-model quality at 1.85x (WMT), 1.89x (CNN/DM), 1.18x (XSum); can exceed it
speed: 1.85x WMT, 1.89x CNN/DM, 1.18x XSum latency reduction at large-model quality (T5, T=1, γ=5, bs1)
datasets: WMT En-De, CNN/DM, XSum, GSM8K, MBPP, SQuAD 2.0, WebQuestions, NaturalQA, TriviaQA

method: draft model writes each reasoning step; PRM scores it; keep if reward ≥ δ (0.7), else regenerate the step with the target
upside: spends target compute only on low-reward steps; reward bias can raise accuracy
method_downside: lossy: biased toward high-reward steps, not the target distribution; needs a step-level PRM (none for general domains); δ tuned per task; third model in memory
memory: draft (~1.5B) + PRM (1.5B-7B, Skywork-o1-PRM) + both KVs; README needs ≥3 GPUs in vLLM online mode
quality: lossy (gain): +1.1 avg accuracy vs target over 6 benchmarks; GPQA-Diamond 38.4 vs 32.8
speed: up to 4.4x fewer FLOPs vs target-only; wall-clock not reported (A100, vLLM)
llama_results: Llama-3.1-8B target with ~1B Llama draft tested; numbers not seen

method: small model writes each step; large model scores utility 0-9 in a prefill pass; keep if ≥7 else large model regenerates; stacks with token-level SD
upside: offloads easy steps to a 1.5B model; scoring is prefill-only, cheaper than generation
method_downside: lossy: output mostly small-model text, not the target's; static score threshold; each step needs a large-model prefill; both models colocated with statically split KV
memory: R1-Distill-1.5B + its KV colocated with 32B base
quality: lossy (gain, v1): +1.0 MATH500, +3.1 AIME, +9.9 GPQA vs QwQ-32B
speed: v1: 2.5x MATH500, 1.9x AIME, 1.5x GPQA (QwQ-32B, 2xA6000, vLLM 0.8.2, T=0.6); +19.4-44.2% latency cut over SD alone
llama_results: R1-Distill-Llama-70B as base (§5.4); numbers not seen

method: small reasoning model generates; at '\n\n' + reflective cues ('wait', 'alternatively') the large model writes 20-125 tokens
upside: large model only intervenes at reflection points (~20% of tokens), lifting the small model's accuracy and shortening outputs
method_downside: lossy vs large model: output mostly small-model text; cue words are model-family heuristics; both models must share a family/tokenizer
memory: full large model (14B/32B) + KV alongside the small model
quality: lossy vs 32B (accuracy vs 32B alone not seen); small model gains: MATH500 83.2 -> 89.4, GPQA 33.8 -> 41.9
speed: est. 96.6 vs 32.2 tok/s for 32B alone (FLOP-based estimate, A100-class, not measured)

method: draft model writes n=5 full CoTs in parallel; target picks one in a single forward pass or rethinks if all are wrong; LoRA-tuned draft and target
upside: replaces most target CoT tokens with a single selection pass
method_downside: lossy: output is a draft CoT, not the target's; LoRA tuning of both models (math only); 'all wrong' detected only 52% of the time, wasted drafts when rejected
memory: draft model (1.5B or 8B) + 5 parallel draft KVs (≤5000 tokens each); LoRA merged
quality: lossy: 'near-target' accuracy, exact drop not seen; CollegeMath above target

method: draft proposes γ=6 future steps; target writes each step in one batched pass; LLM judge (Qwen2.5-7B) checks semantic equivalence; accept up to first mismatch; stacks with token SD
upside: step-level parallelism adds a second level on top of token SD, lifting its ceiling
method_downside: lossy: judge false accepts become answer errors; judge model adds memory and latency; steps split on '\n\n' only
memory: draft 1.5B/1.7B + judge 7B (or ~100M embedding model) + batched KV for γ steps; judge on its own GPU
quality: lossy: +1.0 to -2.1 pts vs target AR (GSM8K 92.8 vs 91.8)
speed: LR+SD 1.49-2.11x, LR alone 1.04-1.71x, n-gram SD 1.32-1.53x (32B targets, 8xH100, vLLM 0.8.3, T=0.6)
datasets: GSM8K, AIME24, AMC12-23, HumanEval, LiveCodeBench, GPQA, MT-Bench

method: sample k draft candidates per step, pick most self-consistent (sentence embeddings), accept if attention-grounding + log-prob ensemble score > τ, else target recomputes
upside: step acceptance from model-internal signals, no external PRM
method_downside: lossy: no distribution guarantee; needs attention maps (last 3 layers), at odds with fused attention kernels; k samples per step plus a sentence encoder; τ and β tuned
memory: 1.5B drafter + k=3 candidate KVs + sentence encoder + sparsified attention maps (not reported, est.)
quality: lossy (gain): +3.6% accuracy vs standard SD (target-only MATH500 83.0)
speed: ~11% lower latency vs standard SD (hardware not seen)
